text:
Quinn Hughes was in the middle of a career-long 13-game point streak (6 goals, 15 assists, a Wild record for defensemen) when a hit from Adam Klapka sent him out of a 4-1 win in Calgary on Nov. 19. He has missed both games since, and Minnesota placed him on injured reserve Monday. NHL.com reported that a concussion has been ruled out.

Before that he was doing everything: 34 points in 24 games, 27:49 a night (the most of any skater), and Minnesota taking 57.3% of the expected goals at five on five with him on, 9.4 points better than without him. Evolving-Hockey had him as the most valuable defenseman in the league last season, 4.9 wins above replacement, first among 215.

The goals are the part to take lightly. He has 8 on 4.0 expected, shooting 13% after 4% last season, and our form check calls the recent run mostly bounces. The passing is not a bounce: Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him in the 99th percentile of defensemen for primary shot assists. The first thing to watch is simply when he's back.
